title: Cross-language Fetch & Stream Safety: Clarify SDK surface guarantees for pagination, retries, and stream degradations
creator: Riley Chen
description: Problem statement: Teams building production features on Redwood rely on consistent client semantics across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs for paginated fetches, resumable streaming, and retry behavior. Recent customer reports and internal QA uncovered inconsistencies: differing cursor encodings, incompatible retry backoff semantics, and diverging stream close/error semantics that break resilient integrations and make cross-team library sharing harder. Goal: Produce a clear, actionable, and testable requirements doc that defines the expected SDK contracts for pagination, retries, and streaming semantics; scope a minimal set of API surface changes; and provide acceptance criteria that allow engineering to implement language-specific idiomatic APIs while guaranteeing cross-language compatibility and safe rollouts.
background: Multiple clients and partner integrations (internal dashboards, embeddings pipeline, and third-party connectors) surfaced failures when switching client languages. Example issues: (1) Cursor token formats differed between SDKs, preventing seamless resume across services; (2) The TypeScript SDK treated streaming terminal errors as fatal, tearing down connections where Python attempted best-effort reconnection; (3) Retry windows and idempotency semantics were not explicitly documented, leading to duplicate writes in a small set of customers. The SDK working group proposed a compatibility contract but left many language-specific choices undefined. This PRD clarifies the contract and enumerates acceptance tests and rollout controls.
goals: 1) Define a single canonical cursor/continuation token format (base64-encoded JSON envelope) and a compatibility shim plan for older tokens. 2) Standardize retry semantics: idempotency key behavior, jittered exponential backoff defaults, max-retry-count, and server-side vs client-side retriable error classification. 3) Define streaming lifecycle semantics: onNext/onData, onError semantics (recoverable vs terminal), resume semantics for server streams, and graceful degradation to polling when streaming isn't available. 4) Provide per-language API patterns that are idiomatic but semantically equivalent. 5) Create acceptance criteria and automated language-agnostic tests used in CI.
non_goals: 1) Rewriting existing SDKs entirely; we accept incremental adapter layers where necessary. 2) Changes to server-side token format without backward-compatible shim. 3) Changing server reliability SLAs as part of this ticket.
scope_in: - Canonical cursor envelope spec and migration shim. - Retry policy defaults and APIs to override them. - Streaming semantics contract and a fallback policy to long-polling. - Test harness and CI checks that verify cross-language behavior. - Docs and migration guide for integrators.
scope_out: - New ergonomic helpers for application-level idempotency (separate ticket). - Language runtime performance optimizations unrelated to API semantics. - Documentation translations and external marketing collateral.
personas: - Product engineers integrating Redwood SDKs into services. - Platform/infra engineers building server-side resume and cursor logic. - SDK maintainers in Python/TS/Go who must implement surface changes.
requirements: 1) Cursor format: server will issue a windowed continuation token encoded as base64(JSON) with fields {cursor_version, payload, expiry_ms, sig_version}. SDKs must expose token as opaque string but provide helper utilities to validate expiry and to re-issue server requests with the token. 2) Back-compat: SDKs must accept legacy raw-cursor strings and transform them to the canonical envelope before exposing helper methods. 3) Pagination APIs: - Streaming-capable endpoints must provide two consumer patterns: (a) iterator/async generator (Python/TS) or channel/iterator (Go) for streaming consumption; (b) page-based fetch(page_token, page_size) returning (items, next_page_token). Both patterns must be first-class and consistent across languages. 4) Retry semantics: - Default policy: jittered exponential backoff with base 100ms, multiplier 2, max_interval 5s, max_retries 5. - Retries are only applied to idempotent operations (server marks idempotency via HTTP header or SDK wrapper). - SDKs must provide a pluggable retry policy interface to override defaults. 5) Streaming error model: - Define recoverable errors (transient network 5xx, stream disconnect) vs terminal errors (invalid auth, malformed response). - For recoverable errors the iterator/stream should surface an error object and allow the consumer to call resume(stream_token) where the stream_token is provided periodically (server will include a progress cursor in stream frames). - If resume is not possible or fails, SDK should provide an explicit fallback to page-based polling when configured. 6) Observability hooks: SDKs must emit standardized telemetry events for retries, resume attempts, token expiry, and stream fallback. 7) Compatibility: Public API signatures must be kept semver-major compatible; new behavior should be opt-in behind feature flags when behavior could change existing callers.
language_guidance: Python: - Provide async generator (async for) and sync iterator with identical resume semantics. - Expose helpers: validate_token(token)->bool and refresh_token(token)->token. - Retry policy interface must be a simple dataclass config and a pluggable handler callable. TypeScript: - Provide AsyncIterator + event emitter option for stream consumers. - Expose utilities in top-level exports: isCursorExpired(token): boolean and migrateCursor(legacyToken): string. - Retry overrides via config object passed to client constructor. Go: - Provide channel-based streaming API and a PageFetcher interface for pagination. - Token helpers as simple functions in client package. - Retry policy as an interface allowing DI of backoff strategy.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: All three SDKs accept and expose the canonical token envelope and successfully convert legacy tokens during CI test runs.

AC2: CI harness runs a language-agnostic test that streams a 10-minute simulated stream, injects a transient disconnect, and asserts that resume(stream_token) picks up without data duplication more than once per item.

AC3: Default retry behavior validated in CI across languages using an injected flaky network proxy; retries observe configured max_retries and backoff windows and do not retry non-idempotent endpoints.
AC4: Backwards compatibility: no semver-major changes to public constructors or method names; any breaking opt-in behind a feature flag and documented in migration guide.
AC5: SDKs emit telemetry events and logs for retry attempts, resume attempts, and stream fallback; events conform to the telemetry schema and are validated in an e2e test.
AC6: Documentation: migration guide, per-language examples for resume and fallback, and an operations runbook are published in the SDK docs site and linked from the client changelog.
AC7: Performance: page-based pagination performance remains within 10% of prior median tail latency for common page sizes (10-100) during local benchmarks.
AC8: Rollout: Feature flag gating present and used in canary release before global rollout; must pass canary for two full business days without increased error budget.
AC9: Security: token handling avoids logging raw tokens by default and passes a lightweight manual review for accidental leakage scenarios.

AC10: API parity: examples in all three SDKs produce identical high-level behavior for a reference integration (resume after transient, fallback to polling on terminal failure, and configurable retry policy).
testing_plan: 1) Implement language-agnostic CI tests that drive a mock server simulating stream cursors, transient failures, and token expiry. 2) Inject flaky proxy to validate retry/backoff. 3) Cross-language integration test: use Python consumer to produce a list, TS consumer to resume, and Go consumer to validate page tokens; assert idempotency and non-duplication. 4) Unit tests for helper token migration and token expiry checks. 5) Telemetry validation: unit test telemetry schema and e2e verification pipeline.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Merge SDK adapters behind feature flags, run canary across 5 internal tenants. Phase 2: Enable on all non-production orgs for 48 hours and monitor retry/stream metrics. Phase 3: Gradual enablement on production orgs over two weeks with automatic rollback if error budget breached. Provide migration window and opt-out via client config for 90 days.
docs_and_migration: Deliverables: - migration-guide.md with code samples in Python/TS/Go - API reference updates for new token helpers and retry config - ops runbook for stream resume and fallback behavior - changelog entry detailing default retry changes and opt-in flags
risks: 1) Consumers that depend on current implicit retry behavior may observe different failure modes; mitigation: opt-in gating and clear migration docs. 2) Server-side changes to token envelope could cause partial failure if shims are incomplete; mitigation: server to accept both legacy and envelope formats for 6 months. 3) Test harness complexity and flakiness; mitigation: incremental tests and deterministic fault injection.
open_questions: Q1: Should SDKs attempt automatic resume by default or leave resume to the integrator? (Proposal: default to non-automatic; provide simple opt-in autoResume=true)
Q2: How should we communicate token expiry errors in a way that is actionable across languages? (Proposal: standardized error code and helper isCursorExpired)
Q3: Any special handling required for server-sent events vs websocket vs HTTP chunked streams? (Proposal: abstract stream frame semantics and map transports to the spec in each SDK)
Q4: What is the recommended telemetry sampling rate for high-volume customers to avoid noise? (Proposal: default 1% with override in client config)
Q5: Do we need to provide a migration tool for large-scale legacy token backfills? (Proposal: deferred to a follow-up ticket if customers request)

SDK-TS: add AsyncIterator+Emitter pattern and migration utils (estimate 5 points)

decision_log: 2026-02-25: Chose base64(JSON) envelope for tokens to allow future extensibility. 2026-03-03: Decided to keep automatic resume opt-in after stakeholder feedback from infra and legal. 2026-03-08: Agreed on default retry parameters and that retries only apply to idempotent endpoints.
notes: Make minimal surface changes; prefer adapter modules where possible to avoid breaking consumers.
Coordinate with runtime team to ensure server emits progress cursors at least every 30s for long streams.
Plan a short SDK-only beta with 3 customers who volunteered for early testing.
